Simple rule: never discard a card that could be the next rank of an open tower; discard only when all six signals are not full and the card is a duplicate or a high rank far away. Proposal: signal only when the receiver has a card that is playable right now.

text: I'm going to post one short message to the team with my proposals. The main takeaways are that we discarded too many cards, which cost us points, and that some signals gave away information without helping, plus a few blind plays. Our convention is that a rank signal means play the touched card now, while a suit signal is just information to keep in mind. I also want to remember that the newest card in a signal is the one it refers to.

args.text: Retro game 1: 22/35. Lessons: we discarded 11 cards (costly), 2 misfires, and many signals were redundant. Proposal: (1) A RANK signal (e.g. "3") = the touched card is playable NOW; play it on your turn. (2) A SUIT signal (e.g. "Moss") = info only, keep those cards; play them only when their rank is shown next by a rank signal or the tower is clearly next. (3) If a signalled card is not playable yet, keep it, don't play. (4) Discard only when a slot is a known dead card (duplicate of a lit rank or above every open tower), or when we hold all info and no one can play; avoid blind discards. (5) Before a blind play, count unseen cards: only play if the odds are high. (6) Late game, when a tower's remaining cards are pinned to one slot, signal the rank to force the play. Agree?

I'm going to reply to the team briefly and agree with A01, with a couple of adjustments. In practice the signals were mostly treated as "play now," and both rank and suit signals worked. One thing I'm noting is that a suit signal pointing at a slot seemed to work when that tower's next rank was the one that could be played.

I'm noting that discards were costly and that a blind play led to a second misfire, so I'll post a single concise message wrapping up the lessons.

args.text: A03 retro: I agree with A01's list, with two changes. (a) Signals were mostly used as "play now" and that worked: a suit signal on a tower whose next rank is in the touched slot (A04 "Cobalt" -> my slot 4 Cobalt 1) and a rank signal on a playable rank (A02 "2", A04 "2") both lit cards. Keep both as play-now, and say in the signal which slot is meant. (b) Discards cost us the most: 11 discards, many of them cards we later needed (Moss 4, Cobalt 5). Discard only a card that is provably dead, never to get a signal back for a blind guess. Misfires (Violet 2 blind, Rose 4 blind) came from guesses with under 50% odds; with two strikes left late, a blind play is a loss. Also: a signal resets the no-progress counter, so late game a signal to someone who holds a playable card keeps the round going. For the brain: keep the tower-next rule, add the no-blind-discard rule and the slot-named signal.

A03: A03 proposal for the brain. Signals: 1 signal = "play now": a rank signal about rank R means "your card of rank R that is next on its tower is playable, play it". Suit signal means "this suit's tower is next, play what you hold of it in order". To keep information: a signal given when the receiver's cards are not yet playable is a "hold" hint, so the receiver discards a card they know is not needed. Simple rule: never discard a card that could be the next rank of an open tower; discard only when all six signals are not full and the card is a duplicate or a high rank far away. Proposal: signal only when the receiver has a card that is playable right now.
